```{pyodide}
#| autorun: true
#| edit: false
# The climt wheel is installed by micropip at document setup (before any cell
# runs) via the `pyodide: packages:` block in the page front matter — see
# radiative-transfer/09-live-rce.qmd. Installing here with `await
# micropip.install(...)` instead would race: quarto-live does not await one
# autorun cell's async work before starting the next, so a downstream cell can
# run before the wheel finishes installing. So this cell is synchronous.
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import climt
from sympl import AdamsBashforth
from datetime import timedelta


def integrate_with_snapshots(tendency_components, state, timestep, n_steps,
                             solar, n_snapshots=8, title=""):
    """Step toward radiative equilibrium, recording the evolution, then draw it.

    quarto-live runs each Pyodide cell to completion in a Web Worker and only
    paints the cell's *final* captured figure — so a genuinely live, frame-by-
    frame matplotlib animation is impossible here (an earlier version tried and
    only ever showed the last frame). Instead we run the whole integration
    quietly (the reader sees quarto-live's spinner while it computes; the non-
    grey column takes ~2 min) and, at the end, render one annotated figure that
    shows the *evolution*: temperature / heating / flux profiles at several
    times, plus the top-of-atmosphere longwave flux (OLR) and surface
    temperature as time series approaching energy balance.

    The stepping loop and update order match ``integrate_to_equilibrium`` (the
    native test guards that twin). Only tendency components are used (the RCE
    demo has no stepper-kind components); ``solar`` is the prescribed absorbed
    shortwave (W m^-2), drawn as the equilibrium target on the OLR panel.
    """
    model = AdamsBashforth(list(tendency_components))
    p = state["air_pressure"].values[:, 0, 0] / 100.0
    p_int = state["air_pressure_on_interface_levels"].values[:, 0, 0] / 100.0
    day = timestep.total_seconds() / 86400.0

    # Snapshot the full profiles at ~n_snapshots evenly spaced steps (from the
    # first step, once the radiation diagnostics are populated, to the last).
    snap_at = set(np.unique(
        np.linspace(1, n_steps, n_snapshots).round().astype(int)).tolist())
    snaps = []              # profile snapshots (a handful)
    days, olr, tsurf = [], [], []   # cheap scalars recorded every step

    for i in range(1, n_steps + 1):
        diagnostics, new_state = model(state, timestep)
        state.update(new_state)
        state.update(diagnostics)
        state["time"] += timestep
        days.append(i * day)
        # OLR = upwelling longwave flux at the top interface (index -1 = TOA).
        olr.append(float(state["upwelling_longwave_flux_in_air"].values[-1, 0, 0]))
        tsurf.append(float(state["surface_temperature"].values.ravel()[0]))
        if i in snap_at:
            snaps.append(dict(
                day=i * day,
                T=state["air_temperature"].values[:, 0, 0].copy(),
                H=state["air_temperature_tendency_from_longwave"].values[:, 0, 0].copy(),
                U=state["upwelling_longwave_flux_in_air"].values[:, 0, 0].copy(),
                D=state["downwelling_longwave_flux_in_air"].values[:, 0, 0].copy(),
            ))

    _draw_evolution(snaps, np.array(days), np.array(olr), np.array(tsurf),
                    solar, p, p_int, title)
    return state


def _draw_evolution(snaps, days, olr, tsurf, solar, p, p_int, title):
    """Render the RCE evolution as one annotated 2x2 figure (browser-only)."""
    cmap = plt.get_cmap("viridis")
    norm = plt.Normalize(vmin=snaps[0]["day"], vmax=snaps[-1]["day"])

    fig = plt.figure(figsize=(11.5, 8.4))
    gs = fig.add_gridspec(2, 2, hspace=0.34, wspace=0.30)
    ax_T = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 0])
    ax_H = fig.add_subplot(gs[0, 1], sharey=ax_T)
    ax_F = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 0], sharey=ax_T)
    ax_O = fig.add_subplot(gs[1, 1])

    n = len(snaps)
    for k, s in enumerate(snaps):
        c = cmap(norm(s["day"]))
        final = (k == n - 1)
        w = 2.6 if final else 1.3
        z = 5 if final else 2
        ax_T.plot(s["T"], p, color=c, lw=w, zorder=z)
        ax_H.plot(s["H"], p, color=c, lw=w, zorder=z)
        ax_F.plot(s["U"], p_int, color=c, lw=w, zorder=z)
        ax_F.plot(s["D"], p_int, color=c, lw=w, ls="--", zorder=z)

    ax_T.set_ylabel("pressure (hPa)"); ax_F.set_ylabel("pressure (hPa)")
    ax_T.set_xlabel("temperature (K)"); ax_T.set_title("Temperature profile")
    ax_H.set_xlabel("LW heating rate (K day$^{-1}$)")
    ax_H.set_title("Longwave heating rate")
    ax_F.set_xlabel("LW flux (W m$^{-2}$)")
    ax_F.set_title("LW flux: up (solid) / down (dashed)")
    ax_T.invert_yaxis()                     # shared y inverts all three profiles
    for ax in (ax_T, ax_H, ax_F):
        ax.grid(alpha=0.3)
    ax_H.axvline(0.0, color="0.4", lw=0.8)

    # Annotations that explain what the reader is looking at.
    T_final = snaps[-1]["T"]
    ax_T.annotate("warm surface", xy=(T_final[0], p[0]),
                  xytext=(0.42, 0.14), textcoords="axes fraction", fontsize=8,
                  arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="0.3"))
    ax_T.annotate("isothermal top\n(skin temperature)", xy=(T_final[-1], p[-1]),
                  xytext=(0.30, 0.72), textcoords="axes fraction", fontsize=8,
                  arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="0.3"))
    ax_H.text(0.04, 0.06, "cooling (< 0) aloft\nrelaxes toward 0\nat equilibrium",
              transform=ax_H.transAxes, fontsize=8, va="bottom")
    ax_F.text(0.55, 0.9, "surface emits up;\nspace sends nothing down",
              transform=ax_F.transAxes, fontsize=8, va="top")

    sm = plt.cm.ScalarMappable(norm=norm, cmap=cmap); sm.set_array([])
    cbar = fig.colorbar(sm, ax=[ax_T, ax_H, ax_F], location="right",
                        fraction=0.02, pad=0.02)
    cbar.set_label("time (days)  —  early (dark) → late (yellow)")

    # OLR / surface-temperature time series: the march toward energy balance.
    ax_O.plot(days, olr, color="#c92a2a", lw=1.9, label="OLR (top of atmosphere)")
    ax_O.axhline(solar, color="0.35", ls="--", lw=1.2,
                 label=f"absorbed solar = {solar:.0f} W m$^{{-2}}$")
    ax_O.set_xlabel("time (days)")
    ax_O.set_ylabel("longwave flux (W m$^{-2}$)", color="#c92a2a")
    ax_O.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor="#c92a2a")
    ax_O.set_title("Approach to energy balance")
    ax_O.grid(alpha=0.3)

    ax_Ts = ax_O.twinx()
    ax_Ts.plot(days, tsurf, color="#1c7ed6", lw=1.6)
    ax_Ts.set_ylabel("surface temperature (K)", color="#1c7ed6")
    ax_Ts.tick_params(axis="y", labelcolor="#1c7ed6")

    gap = solar - olr[-1]
    msg = (f"still {gap:+.0f} W m$^{{-2}}$ from balance\n(raise N_STEPS to close it)"
           if abs(gap) > 2 else "OLR ≈ absorbed solar:\nnear equilibrium")
    ax_O.annotate(msg, xy=(days[-1], olr[-1]), xytext=(0.12, 0.30),
                  textcoords="axes fraction", fontsize=8,
                  arrowprops=dict(arrowstyle="->", color="0.3"))
    ax_O.legend(loc="lower right", fontsize=7)

    if title:
        fig.suptitle(title, fontsize=13, y=0.98)
    plt.show()


def integrate_to_equilibrium(tendency_components, stepper_components, state,
                             timestep, n_steps):
    """Step tendency + stepper components forward toward radiative equilibrium.

    Keep this body in sync with the copy in
    docs/radiative-transfer/_live/rce_helpers.py.

    Update order matters: the new (prognostic) state is applied *before* the
    diagnostics, so flux diagnostics (e.g. the longwave fluxes SlabSurface
    consumes) survive into the next step instead of being clobbered by the
    stepper carrying those fields forward at their pre-step value.
    """
    model = AdamsBashforth(list(tendency_components))
    for _ in range(n_steps):
        diagnostics, new_state = model(state, timestep)
        state.update(new_state)
        state.update(diagnostics)
        for stepper in stepper_components:
            s_diag, s_new = stepper(state, timestep)
            state.update(s_new)
            state.update(s_diag)
        state["time"] += timestep
    return state


# End on a plain statement (not a def): quarto-live captures each cell's final
# value for display, and marshalling a bare function object through JS interop
# yields an unhashable JsProxy that aborts the cell.
print("climt", climt.__version__, "ready — has_fortran:", climt.has_fortran_extensions())
```
